item.title: The Unequal Economic Consequences of Carbon Pricing
item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 79.9 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

This paper studies the economic impacts of carbon pricing. Exploiting institutional features of the European carbon market and high-frequency data, I identify carbon policy shocks and trace their dynamic effects. A restrictive carbon policy shock raises energy prices, reduces emissions, spurs green innovation, but decreases economic activity—disproportionately burdening poorer households. Not only are the poor more affected because of their higher energy spending, but they also experience larger income losses. These indirect, general equilibrium effects via income and employment play an important role in the transmission of carbon pricing policies, accounting for about two-thirds of the aggregate consumption response. (JEL E23, E24, O44, Q41, Q54, Q55, Q58)

item.title: The Causal Effects of Global Supply Chain Disruptions on Macroeconomic Outcomes: Evidence and Theory
item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 54.9 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

We study the causal effects of global supply chain disruptions by constructing a new index of real-time port congestion using Automatic Identification System data from container ships and a spatial clustering algorithm. We develop a model with search frictions between producers and retailers that links upstream production slack to downstream supply shortages and captures output and price responses to supply chain shocks. The co-movements of output, prices, spare capacity, and market tightness provide novel identification restrictions. We find that demand and supply shocks drove US disinflation in 2020, while the inflation surge in 2021 was driven mainly by supply chain shocks. (JEL C43, E31, F14, F23, L14, L92)

item.title: The Inflation Attention Threshold and Inflation Surges
item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 52.8 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

The recent inflation surge brought inflation back on people's minds. I quantify when and how much attention to inflation changes and derive the macroeconomic implications of these attention changes. I estimate an attention threshold at an inflation rate of 4 percent, that attention doubles when inflation exceeds this threshold, and that supply shocks have stronger and more persistent effects on inflation in times of high attention. Developing a model featuring the attention threshold, I show that attention changes offer a joint explanation for inflation surges, inflation's co-movement with inflation expectations, and a long last mile of disinflation. (JEL D84, E12, E31, E43, E52)

item.title: Union Bargaining Power and the Amenity-Wage Trade-Off
item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 51.0 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

This paper studies how collective bargaining affects wages and amenities. By merging collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) to linked employer-employee data in Brazil, I combine rich contracted amenities with wage information. I implement a difference-in-differences strategy that exploits a court ruling enforcing CBA continuation (i.e., ultra-activity) to estimate the effects of union bargaining power. Strengthening unions raises wages and amenities without reducing employment—increasing retention despite some labor-labor substitution. A revealed-preference approach shows that amenities account for 45 percent of total compensation gains. These findings suggest that collective bargaining can offset monopsony power, but employers retain the right-to-manage workforce composition. (JEL J31, J32, J42, J51, J52, O15)

item.title: Inequality and Racial Backlash: Evidence from the Reconstruction Era and the Freedmen's Bureau
item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 37.4 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

How do majority groups respond to narrowing inequality in racially polarized environments? We study this by examining the Freedmen's Bureau, an agency created after the US Civil War to aid former slaves and launch institutional reform in the South. Using new historical records and an event-study approach, we estimate the bureau's impact on political, social, and economic outcomes. Vote shares for Democrats, the party that previously championed slavery and opposed Black civil rights, initially eroded in bureau counties, but these impacts faded as federal oversight weakened. Racial backlash emerged rapidly and persisted, suggesting White majorities sought to offset Black progress. (JEL D63, D72, J15, N31, N41)

item.title: The Effects of School Phone Bans: National Evidence from Lockable Pouches
item.description:
The Quarterly Journal of Economics ｜ 综合分 37.4 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前）

Abstract Schools across the U.S. have sharply restricted student use of phones during the school day. We evaluate one type of restriction—lockable phone pouches—using nationwide data combining a large-scale teacher survey, GPS pings, standardized test scores, and school administrative records, along with sales records from the largest pouch provider. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that pouch adoption substantially reduces phone use as measured by GPS pings and teacher reports. In the first year after adoption, disciplinary incidents increase, and we find suggestive evidence that student subjective well-being falls, consistent with short-term disruption. However, disciplinary effects fade, while the estimated effects on well-being appear to recover and become positive in later years. For academic achievement, average effects on test scores are consistently close to zero. High schools see modest positive effects, particularly in math, while middle schools see small negative effects. We find little evidence of effects on school attendance and no clear evidence of improvements in self-reported classroom attention or perceived online bullying.

item.title: The Returns to Government R&D: Evidence from US Appropriations Shocks
item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 37.4 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

Based on a narrative classification of all significant postwar changes in R&D appropriations for five major federal agencies, we find that an increase in nondefense R&D appropriations leads to increases in various measures of innovative activity and higher business-sector productivity in the long run. We structurally estimate the production function elasticity of nondefense government R&D capital using the SP-IV methodology of Lewis and Mertens (2024) and obtain implied returns of 140 to 210 percent over the postwar period. The estimates indicate that government-funded R&D accounts for one-fifth of business-sector TFP growth since WWII and imply substantial underfunding of nondefense R&D. item.title: Firm Adaptation in Production Networks: Evidence from Extreme Weather Events in Pakistan
item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 37.1 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

This paper considers how far private adaptation may reduce future vulnerability to climate risks. Using data on monthly firm-to-firm transactions from Pakistan, we find that flood-affected firms are more likely to relocate to safer ground and shift purchases toward suppliers in less flood-prone regions and reached via less flood-prone roads. The results indicate that firms are imperfectly informed about flood risk and update their beliefs following floods. We quantify aggregate impacts using a spatial model of endogenous production network formation. The findings suggest that firms' learning will shape the economic impact of increasingly frequent climate-related disasters. (JEL D22, L14, O13, O14, Q54, R32)

item.title: The Evolution of the Market for Corporate Control
item.description:
The Journal of Finance ｜ 综合分 35.6 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前）

ABSTRACT We consider an informed large shareholder who can choose between making a takeover bid herself and initiating a sale to another acquirer. Such takeover activism complements direct takeovers because the very choice mitigates the asymmetric information problem, thereby improving efficiency. As more investors enter the market for corporate control, takeover activism increasingly replaces direct takeovers as the prevailing mode of disciplinary control change, matching the evolution in practice. Our model shows how this evolution, characterized by a symbiotic relationship between investor activism and private equity, arises to overcome asymmetric information and collective action problems through intermediated transactions.

item.title: Uncertainty, Volatility, and Renewable Energy Stock Returns: Evidence From Regime‐Dependent and Machine‐Learning Forecasting Models
item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 50.4 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（0 天前） · 在线 2026-10-29

ABSTRACT This study examines the predictability of renewable energy stock returns under economic, financial, and policy uncertainty within a real‐time forecasting framework. Using monthly data from May 2007 to May 2025, we compare conventional econometric models, shrinkage estimators, machine‐learning algorithms, and regime‐dependent forecasting models using a recursive expanding‐window design. Forecast performance is evaluated using statistical accuracy measures, robustness analyses, and an economic portfolio evaluation. The results show that nonlinear forecasting methods consistently outperform conventional linear benchmarks. Gradient boosting achieves the lowest forecast errors, while principal component regression provides stable performance across alternative evaluation designs. Regime‐dependent forecasting models improve directional prediction during periods of heightened financial uncertainty but generate more modest gains in forecast accuracy. Predictor‐importance analysis identifies financial‐market volatility as the dominant source of forecasting information, followed by oil‐market volatility and broader policy uncertainty. Overall, the findings demonstrate that combining multiple sources of uncertainty with flexible forecasting methods improves both statistical forecasting performance and the economic value of investment decisions. JEL Classification: C22 C53 C58 G11 Q42

item.title: Multitype Information Acquisition in a Strategic Trading Model
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 46.5 ｜ 上线 2026-10-29（1 天前）

We analyze information acquisition in a strategic trading model with multidimensional uncertainties. Our main result is that the equilibrium can exhibit multiplicity because of the integer nature of the number of informed traders and the strategic interactions across different types of informed traders. We show that the number of equilibria can be arbitrarily large. Moreover, asymmetric equilibria can arise even in symmetric settings. As information costs rise, fewer traders acquire information, yet prices can become more informative. These results shed light on the instability of financial markets and yield testable empirical predictions. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. item.title: Contest or Contract: Assessing the Effectiveness of Contests in Online Labor Markets
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 38.3 ｜ 上线 2026-10-29（1 天前）

Online labor markets have become increasingly popular among companies seeking global access to workers. Some platforms have adopted a contest-based scheme, allowing employers to review multiple submissions before selecting the best one. This practice raises a crucial question: Given a predefined budget, should employers choose a contest or contract scheme for tasks? This study examines the comparative effectiveness of contests versus contracts in achieving better job outcomes, focusing on design tasks characterized by high uncertainty. Using a comprehensive data set from a leading online labor market, we employ multiple empirical strategies, combined with machine learning and text mining techniques, to examine the impact of compensation schemes on job quality. Our results suggest that contract-based jobs yield better performance than contests in the context of ideation tasks. Further analysis, such as examining image similarity among pairwise solutions within a task, identifies “copying” behaviors as a key mechanism undermining the effectiveness of contests. In the public setting of contests, workers can observe others’ submissions and revise their own, leading to imitation rather than innovation. As competition intensity increases, workers have weaker incentives to exert effort, reducing solution quality. Consequently, the negative incentive effects in contests outweigh both the potential positive incentive and parallel effects. Moreover, although information availability can enhance work quality, contests inherently offer limited informational advantages compared with contracts. Taken together, our findings suggest that contract-based schemes are more effective than contests for design tasks, offering important implications for both employers and platform designers in online labor markets. This paper was accepted by Karan Girotra, operations management. Funding: N. Zhang acknowledges the support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant 72302053]. Supplemental Material: The online appendices and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07082 .

item.title: Inflexibility and Leverage
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 37.6 ｜ 上线 2026-10-29（1 天前）

Firms’ inflexibility to adjust their scale persistently explains capital structure variations in a comprehensive sample and randomly selected subsamples. Higher inflexibility leads to lower financial leverage, potentially due to higher default risk and lower value of tax shields. Contraction inflexibility determines leverage more than expansion inflexibility. Moreover, our inflexibility measure explains financial leverage significantly better than other variables that potentially capture certain aspects of adjustment costs for capital or labor. In addition, inflexible firms increase leverage more following a positive credit supply shock. Analyses employing instrumental variables estimation confirm our main finding. Our results suggest inflexibility shapes corporate financial policies. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. item.title: Do Experimental Asset Market Results Replicate? High‐Powered Preregistered Replications of 17 Key Results
item.description:
The Journal of Finance ｜ 综合分 35.6 ｜ 上线 2026-10-29（1 天前）

ABSTRACT Experimental asset markets provide a controlled approach to studying financial markets. We attempt to replicate 17 key results from four prominent studies, collecting new data from 166 markets with 1,544 participants. Only three of the 14 original results reported as statistically significant were successfully replicated. We fail to replicate findings on emotions, self‐control, and gender differences in bubble formation but confirm that experience reduces bubbles and cognitive skills explain trading success. Our study demonstrates the importance of replications in enhancing the credibility of scientific results in this field.

item.title: Willingness to Compete in Dirty Competitions
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 35.4 ｜ 上线 2026-10-29（1 天前）

Competitive environments often leave room for “dirty” practices such as sabotage, retaliation, or dishonesty. We use an online experiment to document aggregate levels and individual differences in the willingness to engage in dirty competition and in the willingness to enter competitions where the opponent may play dirty. We then use the experimental data to validate a set of survey questions that capture willingness to engage in dirty competition above general willingness to compete. We elicit these questions in a representative survey panel and show that willingness to engage in dirty competition is a strong predictor of holding a management or supervisory position and of working in the private—versus the public—sector, but also of worse self-esteem, worse social relationships, and increased feelings of guilt and shame. Men, younger people, and lower-educated people are on average more willing to engage in dirty competition. This paper was accepted by Dorothea Kübler, behavioral economics and decision analysis. item.title: Correlated Demand Shocks and Asset Pricing
item.description:
Review of Financial Studies ｜ 综合分 68.1 ｜ 上线 2026-10-28（1 天前）

Abstract I propose a mechanism through which institutional investors’ correlated demand shocks provide a source of market risk in asset pricing. Institutional investors have mandates to beat a similar market index. During periods of strong stock market performance, their incentive to outperform intensifies as more of them fall short of the market index. This incentive induces procyclical risk-taking behavior, generating correlated demand that elevates the market betas and risk premia of exposed stocks. Quasi-experiments using exogenous changes in index membership support a causal interpretation of the mechanism. Elevated betas are associated with a higher perceived cost of capital and reduced firm investment. (JEL G1, G2)

item.title: From Employer Responsibility to Environmental Irresponsibility: Unintended Impacts of Social Insurance Law on Pollution Emissions
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 57.6 ｜ 上线 2026-10-28（1 天前）

This study investigates the unintended effect of the introduction of the 2011 Social Insurance Law on corporate pollution emissions. Using a difference-in-differences framework, our analysis reveals that enhanced social insurance contributions lead to higher industrial pollution emissions, as measured by chemical oxygen demand and wastewater emissions. The mechanism analysis indicates that the enforcement of the law increases firms’ labor costs and financial distress, motivating them to reduce efforts on end-of-pipe treatment activities and measures taken during the production process, which results in higher pollution emission intensity. Our study highlights the potential conflict between employee protection and corporate environmental goals. Further analysis suggests that stronger environmental monitoring and environmental, social, and governance disclosure requirements can partially mitigate this tradeoff, providing valuable insights for policymakers. item.title: Estimating the Pricing Kernel: A Simple Regression-Based Dimension-Reduction Approach
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 46.5 ｜ 上线 2026-10-28（1 天前）

We propose a simple framework for estimating the pricing kernel in factor space by constructing the mean–variance efficient factor portfolio via an ordinary least squares formulation with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regularization. The method accommodates high-dimensional settings in which the number of candidate factors exceeds the sample size and automatically shrinks redundant factor weights toward zero. We show theoretically that the out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of the estimated portfolio converges to the theoretical maximum at the fastest rate among existing regression-based approaches. Applying the method to 174 characteristic-based factors together with the market factor, we obtain an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of 3.59, substantially outperforming competing strategies and delivering the smallest aggregate pricing errors. The selected factors vary over time in both composition and number, averaging about 50. We further develop a model comparison test and reject the hypothesis that eight widely used sparse factor models are sufficient to span the pricing kernel. This paper was accepted by Kay Giesecke, finance. item.title: Robust Auction Design with Support Information
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 35.8 ｜ 上线 2026-10-28（1 天前）

A seller wants to sell an item to n buyers. Buyer valuations are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) according to a distribution unknown to the seller; the seller only knows that the support is included in [a, b]. To be robust, the seller chooses a dominant strategy incentive compatible mechanism that optimizes the worst-case performance relative to the ideal expected revenue the seller could have collected with knowledge of buyers’ valuations. Our analysis unifies the regret and the ratio objectives. For these objectives, we derive an optimal mechanism and the corresponding performance in quasi-closed form, as a function of the support information [a, b] and the number of buyers n. Our analysis reveals three regimes of support information and a new class of robust mechanisms. (i) When a/b is below a threshold, the optimal mechanism is a second-price auction (SPA) with random reserve, a focal class in earlier literature. (ii) When a/b is above another threshold, SPAs are strictly suboptimal, and an optimal mechanism belongs to a class of mechanisms we introduce, which we call pooling auctions (POOL); whenever the highest value is above a threshold, the mechanism still allocates to the highest bidder, but otherwise the mechanism allocates to a uniformly random buyer, that is, pools low types. (iii) When a/b is between two thresholds, a randomization between SPA and POOL is optimal. We also characterize optimal mechanisms within nested central subclasses of mechanisms: standard mechanisms that only allocate to the highest bidder, SPA with random reserve, and SPA with no reserve. We show strict separations in terms of performance across classes, implying that deviating from standard mechanisms is necessary for robustness. Lastly, we show that the same results hold under other distribution classes that capture “positive dependence,” namely i.i.d., mixture of i.i.d., and exchangeable and affiliated distributions, as well as i.i.d. regular distributions. This paper was accepted by David Simchi-Levi, revenue management and market analytics. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.02703 .

Their reliance on empirical patterns, however, is also their limitation: these tools can only be applied where data are abundant. I exploit the variation in prior data availability to compare areas in which the tool was usable to those in which it was not. I find that the tool increased the quantity of research in data-rich areas: the resulting output yielded limited biological insights but was methodologically rigorous and contributed to downstream research. item.title: Dual‐Rule Logical Neural Network for Explainable Credit Scoring
item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 33.9 ｜ 上线 2026-10-27（1 天前） · 在线 2026-10-26

ABSTRACT Credit scoring requires modeling complex nonlinear relationships between borrower characteristics and default risk, yet highly expressive predictive models often suffer from limited transparency and weak generalization on small‐scale financial datasets. To address this challenge, this study proposes an interpretable Dual‐Rule Logical Neural Network (DLNet) for credit risk assessment. DLNet first converts continuous features into explicit binary threshold conditions, and then learns risk patterns through differentiable logical operators that explicitly construct conjunctive and disjunctive rule structures. To further improve rule compactness and readability, an explicit logic‐level sparse regularization term is imposed on the continuous logical weights during training, encouraging concise logical connections without penalizing the final prediction layer. In addition, a local rule backtracking extractor is developed to generate instance‐level explanations by tracing the top‐contributing activated logical nodes back to their corresponding threshold or categorical conditions. Experiments on four real‐world credit datasets show that DLNet achieves competitive predictive performance while providing both global rule patterns and local sample‐specific rationales. The learned rules further reveal heterogeneous logical structures across datasets, with disjunctive, conjunctive, and atomic patterns all appearing among high‐contribution rules. These results demonstrate that DLNet offers a practical framework for combining predictive effectiveness, structural sparsity, and decision transparency in credit scoring.

item.title: Selection into Financial Education and Effects on Portfolio Choice
item.description:

We study the impact of a financial education program on portfolio choices in a setting that allows us to examine both participation decisions and differences in program benefits across individuals. We directly elicit willingness to pay for financial education and show that individuals with higher financial literacy, greater confidence in applying new knowledge, and higher expected returns are willing to pay more. Using incentivized portfolio allocation tasks, we develop outcome measures tailored to individual risk preferences and show that financial education improves decision quality along these dimensions. The program increases the share of participants who experience an improvement by 20 percentage points, corresponding to average gains of 3.2 percentage points of initial wealth. Individuals with the highest willingness to participate benefit disproportionately from the program, with important implications for the design and evaluation of financial education initiatives. By isolating a specific investment skill in a setting with voluntary participation, our design sheds light on how selection into financial education shapes measured program effects and informs the assessment of broader workplace and public training programs. item.description:

We examine how funding deficit pressures shape the risk-taking of U.S. corporate defined-benefit pension plans and how targeted regulatory relief can mitigate these incentives. Using the 2012 Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act reform, which temporarily eased funding pressure by revising discount rate calculations, we show that plans receiving greater relief significantly reduced their equity allocations and shifted toward safer assets. This derisking was most pronounced among active plans and those sponsored by more financially constrained firms. Our findings demonstrate that targeted regulatory relief can curb risk-taking incentives even without altering underlying economic conditions or financial reporting standards and shed light on the likely (and unlikely) frictions driving such behavior. item.title: The Equity Market Implications of the Retail Investment Boom
item.description:

We quantify the equilibrium impact of retail traders on the U.S. equity market within a structural model of asset demand. Estimating investor-specific demand curves, we find that Robinhood traders are fundamentally distinct from all other investors, including other households: their demand is the most elastic and tilts most strongly toward volatile and microcap stocks. Each dollar invested through Robinhood generates more than five dollars in aggregate equity repricing, exceeding hedge funds, other households, and all other investor types. We decompose the cross-sectional variation in stock returns during Robinhood’s growth surge in 2020 into investor-specific components and find that shifts in Robinhood traders’ latent demand drove 11% of small-cap return volatility despite their negligible aggregate wealth share. To explain these demand shifts, we show that Robinhood traders are the only investor group whose latent demand is well explained by attention proxies: their demand exhibits a V-shaped response to past returns and rises sharply with trading volume. Our findings suggest that the growth of retail trading platforms represents a fundamental shift in the composition of equity demand with equilibrium consequences disproportionate to retail investors’ share of aggregate wealth. item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 33.6 ｜ 上线 2026-10-26（1 天前） · 在线 2026-10-25

ABSTRACT We develop Galerkin–ARIMA, a projection‐based forecasting framework that expands observation‐ and innovation‐lag states with finite basis functions while nesting classical multiplicative SARIMA as a restricted linear specification. The model is estimated using preliminary residual proxies followed by a joint least‐squares or ridge regression, which supports efficient rolling refitting. For the fixed‐dimensional unpenalized estimator, we establish asymptotic normality while accounting explicitly for generated regressors. Across 10 US macroeconomic and financial series, Galerkin–ARIMA has competitive one‐step‐ahead forecast accuracy, with nonlinear gains varying across series and the linear specification providing the most stable performance. In pre‐specified runtime experiments on Real GDP, the S&P 500, and the Unemployment Rate, Ridge Galerkin–ARIMA is substantially faster than likelihood/state‐space SARIMA under fixed, initially tuned, and repeatedly retuned rolling specifications. The results suggest that the main value of the framework is flexible lag‐state modeling and computationally efficient forecasting. Nonlinear enrichment does not produce uniform accuracy gains.

item.title: Looking Under the Hood of Commodity Currency Predictability
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 66.1 ｜ 上线 2026-10-23（1 天前）

This paper revisits the exchange rate predictability of commodity currencies through the lens of market efficiency. Focusing on currencies with strong contemporaneous exposure to commodity prices, we show that changes in country-specific commodity export or import prices predict exchange rate fluctuations both in sample and out of sample. We establish four empirical facts: (i) the sign of the predictive relationship runs counter to standard risk-based explanations; (ii) predictability is concentrated at short horizons; (iii) predictability is driven by a small set of thinly traded currencies; and (iv) even sophisticated speculative traders adjust positions sluggishly in response to commodity price shocks in these currencies. Together, these findings suggest that predictability arises from the slow incorporation of information in less actively traded currencies, which is likely due to liquidity and position-building constraints, rather than from compensation for risk. The results also clarify the sources of commodity-based predictability in carry trade returns. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. item.title: Bargaining and Contract Forms in Distribution Channels: Why Do Slotting Fees Arise and Linear Contracts Persist?
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 48.6 ｜ 上线 2026-10-23（1 天前）

Two empirical patterns emerge in business-to-business settings, particularly in retail distribution channels such as grocery markets. First, linear contracts are widely observed alongside nonlinear contracts with fixed payments, despite the claimed efficiency advantages of the latter. Second, when fixed payments arise, they often flow from suppliers to retailers (slotting fees) rather than the reverse. We develop and analyze a model of multilateral bargaining in which a supplier negotiates separately with competing retailers to explain these patterns. The key mechanism is a trade-off between two distortions: under linear contracts, wholesale prices reflect bargaining power and can be either above or below the channel-profit-maximizing level, whereas under two-part tariffs, wholesale prices are set to maximize bilateral surplus independently of bargaining power but are systematically too low from an overall channel perspective because of rent shifting across relationships. As a result, neither contractual form uniformly dominates; instead, relative performance depends on how bargaining shapes gains from trade across firms. When bargaining leads to slotting fees, two-part tariffs yield higher channel profits than linear contracts, whereas when it would imply payments from retailers to suppliers, linear contracts may perform better. These findings offer a unified explanation for the persistence of linear contracts alongside two-part tariffs, the direction of fixed payments, and the conditions under which each contractual form is likely to arise. item.description:

ABSTRACT We derive bounds on the rational variation in option‐implied beliefs about market returns. While risk preferences distort option‐implied (or risk‐neutral ) beliefs away from subjective beliefs, one can nonetheless bound risk‐neutral belief movement under a general assumption on the stochastic discount factor. The resulting test requires no knowledge of the objective distribution and allows significantly more flexibility in discount rates than standard volatility tests. item.description:

We examine how users respond to winning symbolic awards in online crowdsourcing contests. Our setting is a machine learning competition platform that grants symbolic medals to recognize participants’ contest achievements. Employing a regression discontinuity design, we find that gold medal winners participate less in subsequent contests but engage more in prosocial activities, evidenced by a greater volume and length of posts, as well as more substantial and frequent code contributions. In contrast, bronze and silver medals do not seem to exert a significant influence on recipients’ subsequent behaviors. Drawing on self-determination theory and the needs-as-motives hypothesis, we provide evidence that need-driven goal shifting plays an important role in driving the dual effects of gold medals—diminished contest participation but enhanced prosocial contributions. Further analyses reveal that winners with previous competition medals are more likely to favor contributing content over competing again, whereas winners with more prior contribution medals are less inclined to further increase contributions. Moreover, team winners exhibit a lower tendency than solo winners to shift their efforts from competition to contribution. We add to the symbolic awards literature by uncovering a novel goal-shifting effect induced by contest medals, where award receipt redirects user effort from the focal rewarded domain to other forms of platform engagement. How does information transparency affect customer retention in markets where quality is difficult to verify? Conventional wisdom suggests that transparency intensifies price competition and increases customer churn. We challenge this view by showing that acquisition-stage transparency can strengthen retention in markets for credence goods characterized by delayed feedback and persistent uncertainty, where customers revisit their decisions without clear quality signals. Analyses of boundary conditions indicate that the retention effect of transparency is amplified when public and private signals remain congruent with earlier informational cues. These findings reconceptualize transparency as a relational mechanism that fosters decisional assurance and stabilizes retention under quality uncertainty. With the rapid expansion of online food delivery (OFD) platforms, subscription models have emerged as a strategic tool to retain users and shape consumption behavior. Despite their growing prevalence, the broader impacts of these subscriptions—both within the OFD sector and across downstream consumer activities—remain underexplored. Overall, this study offers novel insights into how subscription models in physical service platforms can expand market demand, foster crosschannel engagement, and generate positive spillovers in adjacent sectors. The findings offer actionable guidance for platform designers and policymakers to enhance consumer welfare and support local economic vitality. They also provide new evidence for restaurants that additional platform usage costs may be offset by latent economic benefits from heightened consumer engagement. This paper was accepted by D. J. item.title: How New Products Enter Markets: Social Networks, Consumer Imports, and Retailer Learning
item.description:
The Quarterly Journal of Economics ｜ 综合分 35.3 ｜ 上线 2026-10-20（3 天前） · 在线 2026-10-22

Abstract This paper studies how new varieties enter markets and become locally available. We provide causal evidence of demand externalities that operate in two steps. First, information about new varieties diffuses directly through real-world social ties among consumers. Second, early purchases generate an indirect spillover to firms: local retailers learn from “pioneer” consumers which new varieties are most likely to succeed and adjust their product offerings accordingly. We study this process in the context of direct-to-consumer imports. Using customs records on individuals’ purchases matched to population-wide social networks, international migrant links, and retailer catchment areas, we document economically meaningful demand externalities. Product-specific expenditure shocks abroad transmit through migrant networks and shift which varieties consumers purchase. Leveraging these shocks as a plausibly exogenous source of local demand variation, we show strong peer effects: prior purchases by close neighbors, coworkers, or friends increase an individual’s likelihood of purchasing the same variety, especially for premium and visible goods. We leverage this result to identify an indirect spillover from consumers to firms: retailers are more likely to add a variety to their assortment when it becomes popular among consumers in their catchment area. Combining the instrument with linked consumer–retailer data and a self-conducted retailer survey, we show that this response reflects learning about latent demand for varieties not yet stocked locally. Together, social diffusion and retailer learning generate demand multipliers that reshape local product availability and expand access to global variety.

Abstract Intensifying climate change makes protection against natural disaster risk – either through ex ante insurance or ex post aid – a first-order public policy issue. Abstract Agricultural marketing cooperatives are widely viewed as a mechanism for mitigating oligopsony power in agricultural procurement markets. However, the welfare effects of cooperatives depend on how competing investor‐owned firms respond, and those responses vary with the strategic flexibility available to firms. This paper studies how spatial price discrimination and endogenous location mediate the market and welfare effects of cooperatives in spatial procurement markets. Using a structured counterfactual framework, we compare markets with only investor‐owned firms and mixed markets with both investor‐owned firms and cooperatives across four strategic environments defined by the availability of these strategic margins. This attenuation arises because strategic flexibility increases efficiency in benchmark markets with only investor‐owned firms, leaving less scope for cooperatives to improve market performance. Consequently, strategic flexibility and cooperative ownership emerge as partially substitutable mechanisms for improving procurement‐market performance. Cooperatives therefore deliver their largest welfare gains where competing firms face greater strategic constraints arising from regulation, technology, or physical limitations.

To comply with increasingly stringent international standards in risk management and regulation, several approaches have been developed in the literature for forecasting tail-risk measures such as Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES). However, the accuracy of these measures can be significantly affected by multiple sources of uncertainty, including model misspecification, data limitations and estimation procedures. To address these challenges and enhance the predictive performance of individual models, this study introduces novel forecast combination strategies based on the Model Confidence Set (MCS) methodology. Recent evidence, both in the laboratory and in the wild, suggests that the use of generative artificial intelligence reduces the diversity of content produced. As generative AI penetrates more markets and reaches widespread adoption, should we still expect to see content homogenization? item.description:
The Journal of Finance ｜ 综合分 39.9 ｜ 上线 2026-10-14（2 天前）

ABSTRACT We develop a model to study the efficiency of socially responsible investing (SRI) as a mechanism to control firms' externalities. When SRI is not too popular, responsible investors favor strategies that lead to a concentration of SRI in a subset of firms in the economy. This concentration can mitigate coordination issues in adopting green technologies, but it can also crowd out the green investments of excluded firms and increase the price of green products. In equilibrium, responsible investors continue to favor concentration even as SRI becomes more popular, and concentrate the most when concentration is least desirable.

item.title: AI-Driven Human Task Substitution: Evidence from Google Translate and ChatGPT
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 39.4 ｜ 上线 2026-10-14（2 天前）

We examine how different generations of artificial intelligence (AI) substitute for human knowledge worker tasks, leveraging two sequential natural experiments in the translation industry. We study the introduction of Google Neural Machine Translation (GNMT), a predictive, task-specific AI, as well as ChatGPT, a broad, general-purpose generative AI, in a major online labor market. Distinguishing between analytical tasks (regular translations) and intuitive tasks (transcreations, which require creative and cultural adaptation), we estimate difference-in-differences models on transaction-level data from 2016 to 2017 and 2022 to 2023. We find that GNMT reduced the demand for analytical tasks by economically meaningful magnitudes, while having no detectable effect on intuitive tasks. By contrast, ChatGPT produced substantially larger and more uniform reductions for both analytical and intuitive tasks, indicating a marked expansion in the scope and magnitude of AI substitution. By comparing these two technological shocks within the same labor market, we show that conclusions about which types of human work are resilient to automation do not straightforwardly generalize from predictive to generative AI. item.title: Risk, Specialization, and Covered‐Interest Parity
item.description:
The Journal of Finance ｜ 综合分 45.6 ｜ 上线 2026-10-13（2 天前）

ABSTRACT Prevailing theories of financial intermediation assume an integrated financial sector with frictionless risk‐sharing. However, we identify substantial risk‐sharing frictions linked to intermediary specialization using currency derivatives markets as a laboratory. Using confidential supervisory data covering $25 trillion in daily bank exposures, we document imperfect hedging in banks' FX‐swap intermediation: banks rarely hedge their synthetic dollar lending with maturity‐matched foreign safe assets. Intermediaries specialize in markets in which they have expertise in managing the associated exposures, giving rise to cross‐market variation in deviations from covered‐interest parity. Our results highlight the importance of intermediary specialization and its impact on risk premia.

item.title: Tourism Demand Prediction With Tourist‐Generated Images and Text: An Ensemble Sparse ELM Approach
item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 37.1 ｜ 上线 2026-10-13（1 天前）

ABSTRACT This study examines the predictive value of tourist‐generated images and text for daily tourism demand forecasting. Building on established L 0 ‐regularized extreme learning machine (ELM) formulations and ADMM‐based sparse optimization, we construct an ensemble forecasting framework, termed ES‐ L 0 ‐ELM, that combines image‐derived and textual predictors with numerical variables. The framework integrates sparse output‐weight estimation with model selection and weighted aggregation. Experiments on Jiuzhaigou and Mount Siguniang show that ES‐ L 0 ‐ELM achieves lower forecasting errors than the evaluated benchmarks. On the Jiuzhaigou dataset, it reduces MAPE by 18.66% and 14.33% relative to recent tourism forecasting models BERT‐ELM and TFIDF‐Tran‐ELM, respectively. Image features provide greater predictive gains than text features, whereas their combination yields the best performance. This study provides a sparse ensemble forecasting framework and empirical evidence of the complementary value of tourist‐generated images and text.

item.description:
The Energy Journal ｜ 综合分 33.6 ｜ 上线 2026-10-09（9 天前） · 在线 2026-10-08

This special issue collects six articles that translate economic research into practical guidance for electricity regulators. The articles cover regulated monopoly structure, the economics of regulation after restructuring, electric vehicle integration in constrained distribution networks, distributed backup power and grid reliability, the spatial and temporal variation in the environmental value of renewable energy, and energy justice. Across these domains, legacy regulatory frameworks designed for an earlier technological era now generate predictable distortions. Three themes recur: institutional lag, or the pacing problem; the dispersed and tacit knowledge that no central authority can fully aggregate; and the tension between efficiency and equity. Together, the contributions show that economic analysis can inform the decisions regulators face, provided researchers write for practitioners and practitioners' institutional experience shapes the questions researchers ask. ABSTRACT I show that the recent returns to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing are strongly driven by price impact from flows toward ESG portfolios. Using data on trades, I estimate the market's ability to accommodate ESG flows, which is given by the elasticity of substitution between ESG and other stocks. I show that every dollar flowing toward a representative ESG portfolio increases the market value of ESG stocks by $0.8. The growing institutional flows into the ESG portfolio are the main driver of ESG returns and have caused an annual flow‐driven return of 1.9%. In the absence of flows, ESG stocks would not have outperformed the market from 2012 to 2023.

We analyze consumer surplus when a monopolist can adjust both prices and product qualities across segments, engaging in secondand third-degree price discrimination simultaneously. We characterize the consumer-optimal segmentation and show that it has a striking structure: Consumers with the same value receive the same quality in every segment, though prices differ. Under mild conditions, any segmentation harms consumers if and only if demand is sufficiently more elastic than supply. Hence, potential benefits for consumers depend critically on demand and supply elasticities. These findings have implications for regulatory policy regarding price discrimination and market segmentation. (JEL D42, D83, K21, L12, L15)

item.title: Bayesian Estimation and Forecasting of Constrained Spatial Panel Interval‐Valued Autoregressive Models
item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 20.7 ｜ 上线 2026-10-01（14 天前） · 在线 2026-09-30

ABSTRACT Spatiotemporal interval‐valued data have become increasingly important for modeling uncertainty in complex systems, and related statistical methods and forecasting tools remain underdeveloped. This paper proposes a constrained spatial panel interval‐valued autoregressive model, which ensures mathematical coherence by applying a Mills ratio–based correction and captures the dependence between lower and upper bounds. A Bayesian estimation incorporating prior information is then developed, and a corresponding Metropolis‐within‐Gibbs sampling algorithm is constructed. This algorithm provides a computationally tractable simulation‐based framework for estimating the parameters of the proposed model. Monte Carlo simulations show that the proposed method performs favorably relative to several benchmark approaches in parameter estimation, interval fitting, and forecasting. Applications to air quality and housing price data further demonstrate its ability to model spatiotemporal dependence and interval uncertainty effectively. The results highlight the practical value of the proposed model for analyzing environmental and economic systems characterized by uncertainty.

Abstract We propose a tractable model in which risk, at both the micro and macro levels, is endogenous and driven by incentives. In the model, each firm chooses the mean and the variance of its productivity process, as well as how it covaries with the productivity of other firms. Aggregate risk arises when firms select productivity processes that are correlated with one another. The theory predicts that larger firms and those with lower markups are less volatile and less correlated with aggregate productivity. We find support for these predictions in the data. Through their impact on risk-taking decisions, distortions such as taxes and markups can make GDP more volatile in equilibrium. In a calibrated version of the model, removing distortions significantly reduces GDP volatility.
